newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Gazprom sees output up sharply in 15 years.
newsitem.headline: Russian Gazprom sees output up sharply in 15 years.

text.p: Russia's Gazprom natural gas monopoly plans to increase its annual output by 120-130 billion cubic metres (bcm) in 12 to 15 years, Gazprom chairman Rem Vyakhirev said on Tuesday.
Gazprom, the world's largest gas company, accounts for around 95 percent of Russia's gas output. The company produced 565 bcm in 1996, up 5.2 bcm on 1995's level.
Vyakhirev, quoted by Interfax news agency, said increased output would come from new reserves on the Arctic shelf and on the Yamal Peninsula.

Interfax quoted Fuel and Energy Minister Boris Nemtsov, who is also a first deputy prime minister in charge of restructuring natural monopolies, as saying Gazprom shares were artificially low in price.
"Vyakhirev and I have a dream that Gazprom will be worth $100 billion," he was quoted as saying. Gazprom's current market capitalisation is around $8 billion.
Gazprom would not be broken up, Nemtsov said, adding that the state should use its stakes in such natural monopolies as a "mighty instrument".
